🖥 Six Royan Institute researchers named among the world’s top 2 percent of scientists

📌 In the latest international assessment of researchers’ scientific performance for 2025, six researchers from Royan Institute, affiliated with the Academic Center for Education, Culture and Research (ACECR), have been included in the list of the World’s Top 2% Scientists.

This achievement reflects the continued international scientific presence and research contributions of Royan Institute’s researchers.
​
According to the Public Relations and International Affairs Office of Royan Institute, six researchers from the Institute have been recognized in the latest edition of the World’s Top 2% Scientists list, published on October 7, 2026. The researchers were selected based on their scientific performance and the impact of their research in 2025.
​
The recognized researchers are Dr. Hossein Baharvand, Dr. Mohammad Hossein Nasr-Esfahani, Dr. Mohammad Reza Baghban Islami, Dr. Reza Omrani-Samani, Dr. Masoud Vosough, and Dr. Ashraf Moini.
​
The World’s Top 2% Scientists list is a widely recognized international assessment of researchers’ scientific impact. It is compiled using data from the Scopus citation database in collaboration with Stanford University and published by Elsevier. Researchers across various scientific fields and subfields are evaluated using a range of citation-based and research-performance indicators, including the number of citations, the Hirsch index (h-index), and the composite C-score.
​
The representation of Royan Institute researchers on this list in recent years also highlights the Institute’s sustained scientific capacity. According to the reported figures, five Royan Institute researchers were included in the list in 2023, four in 2024, and five in 2025. In the latest assessment, the number of recognized researchers from Royan Institute has risen to six.
​
The inclusion of Royan Institute researchers in this international assessment underscores their scientific standing and their contributions to knowledge generation and the advancement of biomedical research.
​
Royan Institute extends its congratulations to the recognized researchers and the entire Royan community, wishing them continued success in advancing scientific knowledge, conducting impactful research, and further strengthening the country’s position in the global scientific community.

Jaberi-Ansari arrived in Lamerd on Tuesday morning and inspected a section of the city after visiting the central cemetery to pay homage to the martyrs of the “Ramadan War.”
​
He was accompanied by Seyyed Mousa Mousavi, the parliamentary representative for Mehr and Lamerd; Ali Alizadeh, the governor of Lamerd; and several local officials.
​
On the first day of the second US-Israeli-imposed war on February 28 this year, four locations in Lamerd — including a sports hall, two residential areas, and a hall adjacent to a school — were targeted by enemy missiles, resulting in the martyrdom of 21 people and leaving over 100 others injured, a number of them women and children.
​
Four missiles were said to be used in the attack, releasing 720,000 tungsten pellets upon impact. This kind of weapon is described by experts as being designed for mass casualties. The attack sparked condemnations from many countries.
​
Other items on the agenda of the IRNA CEO’s visit to the province include meeting with the families of martyrs in Lamerd; visiting war-hit areas of Larestan; attending the Lar Administrative Council meeting; visiting the Shiraz International Expo; participating in the Fars Information Council; and meeting with journalists and veteran staff of IRNA.

📡 Iran warns against unilateral measures in global economy

📌 Tehran, IRNA — The deputy for international relations of the Central Bank of Iran warns that unilateral measures can deepen economic fragmentation, increase risks, and fuel uncertainty in the global economy.

Speaking at the G24 meeting of central bank governors and finance ministers in Bangkok, Thailand, on Tuesday, Abolfazl Kodehi stressed the need to strengthen economic cooperation, enhance economic resilience, and reform international institutions to address the consequences of unilateralism.
​
The official noted that globalization has created significant opportunities for many economies over the past decades, but progress in developing international institutions and frameworks has slowed in recent years.
​
Unilateral economic policies undermine global economic cooperation and make the world economy more vulnerable to uncertainty and risks, he added.
​
Kodehi further emphasized regional cooperation’s potential to protect economies from risks arising from global fragmentation, noting that effective institutions and practical frameworks are needed to facilitate trade, investment, financing, and technical cooperation.
​
The 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group will take place October 12 to 18 in Bangkok, Thailand.
